label: Week 38, 2026
recap:
This week was quiet for US AI policy, with 12 bill movements across three jurisdictions and no case updates or federal documents. New Jersey accounted for most of the activity with 7 movements, followed by the United States Congress with 4 and Pennsylvania with 1. These movements reflect changes in status for existing bills, not new introductions or passages.

Where themes could be identified, infrastructure and energy appeared twice, including United States Congress HB8800, touching on data centers and their power demands. Single instances touched on consumer protection and discrimination, seen in New Jersey A5496 concerning algorithmic decisions in areas like credit or housing, criminal law in Pennsylvania HB2771, government use of AI in New Jersey A5483, and privacy and data matters in New Jersey A5502. Six bills in the dataset did not fit a specific theme, rounding out a modest week of activity.

reading.body:
Zero recorded activity across every category means the sources behind this ledger logged no United States AI bill movements, court updates, or federal documents for September 14 to September 20, 2026. That is a statement about the ledger, not about the world.

The uniformity is the notable part. Bills, courts, federal documents, jurisdictions, themes, and agencies all sit at zero at once. A single quiet category is ordinary. Every category quiet in the same week is at least as consistent with a collection gap as with a genuinely eventless period, and the data offers no way to tell the two apart. The record also carries a build timestamp of September 13, the evening before the window opens, so on its face the counts were not assembled as a retrospective over the full week they describe.

For AI specifically, this covers policy and litigation only. It says nothing about compute, buildings, or power. The constraints that bind AI scaling, including substations, generation, interconnection, and construction schedules, appear in no field here. A blank week in bills and dockets is therefore not evidence that the physical buildout paused, and not evidence that it continued. It is silence on a subject the data never addressed.

What remains unknown is whether the sources were searched and returned nothing, or were not searched at all. The data does not say which jurisdictions were checked, which agencies were queried, or what threshold a filing had to meet to be logged. Read the week as an absence of records, and read nothing into it beyond that.
